reply_text:
I found the quoted words on the page, but I'd keep this candidate out: it is a date for a chip going into cars, which is a hardware date, not a forecast about what AI will do.

**1. Is the quote on the page?** Yes, word for word. The page is Nvidia's own corporate blog post wrapping up the GTC Spring 2022 keynote, published 2022-03-22. The sentence sits in a paragraph of its own, right after the Hyperion 9 / DRIVE Atlan paragraph. It is the blog's paraphrase ("…Huang announced"), not Huang's own words, a transcript or a printed Q&A. So even if it were admitted, it would be coverage only.

**2. The admission rule:**
- **Part 1 (role):** passes. Huang was co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia on 2022-03-22.
- **Part 2 (looks forward, about AI):** fails. The words say a customer, BYD, will put Nvidia's DRIVE Orin computer, a chip, into cars starting production in the first half of 2023. That is a hardware adoption and production date. It says nothing about what the AI in those cars will do or how self-driving will be deployed. The rule says "a plain hardware date stays out", and the business forecasts it excludes (order books and the like) are close to this too.
- **Part 3 (date):** passes. "First half of 2023" is a dated stage (due 2023-06-30).
- **Part 4 (source):** coverage only, since the only source is the blog's paraphrase.

**Not already recorded.** None of the recorded files is about BYD. The two from the same day, 2022-03-22 (Hyperion 8 in JLR cars, Hyperion 8 in Mercedes cars), are different claims.

**For the reviewer:** those two Hyperion 8 records were admitted. Hyperion 8 is a whole self-driving platform (sensors, computers and software), while Orin is one chip, which is why I read this one as a hardware date. If those admissions were meant to cover any "Nvidia self-driving hardware in a named carmaker's cars by a date", this one would be borderline instead.
